title: Balanced Binary Tree
description:
Given a binary tree `root`, determine if it is **height-balanced**.

A binary tree is height-balanced if, for **every** node in the tree, the heights of its left and right subtrees differ by at most `1`. An empty tree is considered height-balanced (`true`).
hints: Checking only that the root's left and right subtree heights differ by at most 1 is not enough — every subtree must also be balanced.
A naive top-down check recomputes subtree heights repeatedly in O(n^2) time in the worst case.
Use a bottom-up post-order DFS that returns the subtree height if balanced, or a sentinel like `-1` as soon as an imbalance is found, achieving O(n) time.

examples.explanation: At node 20 heights are (1, 1); at root 3 heights are (1, 2). Every node's subtrees differ in height by at most 1.
At root 1, the left subtree has height 3 while the right subtree has height 1 (difference is 2 > 1).
An empty tree is trivially height-balanced.
